question: Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\{y\in\mathbb{R}:-1<y<1\}$ defined by $f(x)=\frac{x}{1+|x|}$. Establish that $f$ is one-one and onto.
explanation:
Form of the function
For $x\geq0$, $|x|=x$, so $$f(x)=\frac{x}{1+x}$$ For $x<0$, $|x|=-x$, so $$f(x)=\frac{x}{1-x}$$

Verification of one-one property

If $x_1,x_2\geq0$, then $$\frac{x_1}{1+x_1}=\frac{x_2}{1+x_2}$$ Cross multiplication gives $$x_1+x_1x_2=x_2+x_1x_2\Rightarrow x_1=x_2$$ If $x_1,x_2<0$, then $$\frac{x_1}{1-x_1}=\frac{x_2}{1-x_2}$$ Therefore, $$x_1-x_1x_2=x_2-x_1x_2\Rightarrow x_1=x_2$$ If one of $x_1,x_2$ is non-negative and the other is negative, their images have different signs, except that $f(0)=0$ and no negative input has image $0$. Hence, equality of images is impossible in this case. Therefore, $f(x_1)=f(x_2)$ always implies $x_1=x_2$, and $f$ is one-one.
